obligation: G111 -- retile the lowest-occupancy non-GEMV kernels found by G110
what_G110_found: Every non-GEMV kernel dispatches at 6-25% of the threads its own pipeline permits, and none is register-limited. That is 4x to 16x of unused threadgroup width with no hardware reason for it, which made raising TG the obvious first experiment.
why_knobs_rather_than_a_rewrite: The rmsnorm, deltanet-rmsnorm and rope kernels already expose TG as an env knob, so the experiment G110 implies can be run end-to-end WITHOUT writing a kernel. Building first and measuring second would have inverted the order this obligation's own history warns about.

results.knob: incumbent: rmsnorm TG 256, deltanet rmsnorm TG 256

verdict: THE HEADROOM DOES NOT CONVERT. The best arm is dn512 at +0.17%, inside this harness's run-to-run spread, and rms512 is 1.30% SLOWER than the incumbent 256. Tokens are IDENTICAL in every arm. Quadrupling the threadgroup on kernels with 4x of measured headroom buys nothing and can cost.
these_kernels_are_CLOSED_not_rewritten: The acceptance says kernels already near roof are to be DOCUMENTED AS CLOSED rather than rewritten. rmsnorm and deltanet-rmsnorm are at their optimum threadgroup: 256 beats 512 and ties 1024. They are closed on the TG axis.
occupancy_is_not_throughput_confirmed_a_: G094 measured a 5.8x traffic swing at zero rank correlation with time. G111's own prior evidence measured argmax transferring 0 of a 25.9x isolated win. This makes three independent confirmations that a structural headroom measurement does not predict an end-to-end win, and it is why G110 was recorded as a RANKING instrument rather than a budget.
not_measured: The rope arm (HAWKING_ROPE_TG) ran at 16 tokens and 2 pairs while every other arm ran at 24 tokens and 3 pairs, and the matched-config baseline for it failed. Comparing across run configurations is how a false finding gets made, so the rope numbers are EXCLUDED rather than blended in. That axis is unmeasured.
